entries.title: Luke 23:1
segments:
:5
 
Brought him before Pilate. To procure the execution of the death sentence.  The Romans had deprived the Sanhedrin of the power of life and death.  But it was necessary to change the nature of the accusation against Jesus.  The Jewish sentence was for blasphemy; a sentence by Pilate could only result from a conviction for treason to the Roman emperor.  See notes on

Whether the man were a Galilean. The report that Jesus was a Galilean enabled Pilate temporarily to put the responsibility of the trial, from which he strongly desired to escape, upon Herod and to make friendly advances to that ruler, with whom he had quarreled.
 

 
Herod's jurisdiction. Which included Galilee and Perea.
 

 
At Jerusalem. To keep the Passover.
 

 
Exceeding glad. But not righteously so.  It was the pleasure of gratifying his curiosity.
